item.title: Is There a Standard Format for AI Agent Memory? (2026)
item.description: There is no standard format for AI agent memory as of November 2026. A note an agent saves in one tool stays in that tool’s shape: a Markdown file, a cited fact on GitHub’s servers, a labeled block, an extracted sentence with a user_id, a JSONL knowledge graph. Three open proposals try to fix that. None has real adoption yet, so sharing memory between agents today means picking one place all of them can reach.

item.title: GitHub Copilot Memory: What It Stores and Where
item.description:
Copilot Memory is GitHub’s automatic memory for Copilot’s agentic features. It saves two things as Copilot works: repository facts (conventions, architecture decisions, build commands) and user preferences. Each fact stores citations to the code that supports it, Copilot revalidates those citations before using the fact, votes on whether it still holds, and anything that goes 90 days without an upvote expires.

It became generally available on paid Copilot plans on 28 October 2026, per GitHub’s changelog, which also added VS Code, the Copilot app, GitHub Mobile, Slack and Teams as surfaces and introduced Copilot dreaming in public preview. Every fact below comes from GitHub’s Copilot Memory docs, its how-to pages and that changelog, read on 9 November 2026. Two numbers changed since this page was first written in October: the expiry went from 28 days to 90, and the surface list went from four to eight. For how other agents handle the same problem, see AI coding agent memory.

item.title: Codex Memory: AGENTS.md, Memories and Add-ons
item.description:
Codex memory is two built-in layers. AGENTS.md files hold instructions you write, and Codex loads them at the start of every run. Codex memories, off by default, turn useful context from past chats into local files under ~/.codex/memories/. For memory that is searchable, shared across agents or kept on a server, add a hook-based plugin such as Hindsight.

Codex is OpenAI’s coding agent for the terminal, IDE and ChatGPT desktop app. Each session starts with an empty context window, so anything Codex should know must come back in from a file or a tool. Facts below come from OpenAI’s Codex memories docs and AGENTS.md guide, checked 13 October 2026, and from the Codex source and release notes up to 0.166.0 (29 October 2026). For Claude Code, Cursor and Copilot, see AI coding agent memory.
